newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares end firmer on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares end firmer on technical buying.

text.p: Manila shares closed on a firmer tone on Tuesday following a volatile session in which bargain hunters managed to overcome profit-takers, brokers said.
The composite index gained 9.62 points, or 0.34 percent, to close at 2,818.27 mainly due to technical buying. The index was down by as much as 28 points in early trade.
Jidgette Valenzuela, research manager at Lippo Securities, said that buying was mainly technical in nature especially after local shares succumbed to heavy selldown on Monday.
The index skidded 73 points on Monday.
She said the technical buying had warded off likely sellers who might have used the sharp overnight fall in Wall Street as an excuse to sell.

The Dow Jones reacted negatively to a statement made by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto suggesting Japan may turn to large-lot selling of U.S. Treasuries. Hashimoto later said he was misinterpreted.
Allan Araullo, vice president of Regina Capital Development Corp, said major blue chip issues helped keep the index bouyant. Heavyweights PLDT and Petron Corp were among the gainers.

However, the runup was tempered by persistent selling in property counters, especially Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc and its subsidiary Empire East Land Holdings Inc . Both real estate developers had healthy runups late last week.
Valenzuela said the market would continue to remain volatile in the coming days, fluctuating between 2,750 and 2,900, due to the absence of any market moving developments.
"Until clear indications in the corporate front and economic figures emerge, we will continue to see volatility in the market," she said.
